translations.text: A confession by Father Basil, bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, which he delivered concerning the end of the age and the temple of Solomon, and concerning departure from the body.
Let us now understand, brothers, that when God was creating all creation, no one knew.
There was neither sound nor disturbance, but great silence and stillness when he created everything.
We have also heard in the holy Scriptures about the day when heaven and earth will be dissolved. It is written how much turmoil there will be.
For he said that the other angels will work to bring about the dissolution of the world, just as we have heard.
Our Savior has told us in the Gospels about the disturbances, the afflictions, and the earthquakes that will happen.
For he said, “There will be a great affliction unlike anything that has happened since the beginning of the creation of the world, and nothing like it [?] will ever happen again.”
He also says elsewhere, “Heaven and earth will be shaken, and the powers of the heavens will tremble on that day.”
Great earthquakes, trumpet blasts, and great peals of thunder sounding with loud voices.
For the angels were spread out to the four corners of the world,
gathering all humanity together and making them stand before the terrifying judgment seat of the Son of God, separating the ungodly from among the righteous.
Look also at the time when he created everything: no one knew except him and his beloved Son, Jesus Christ.
But when he destroys them, all creation will be shaken, until the last hour and the dissolution of heaven and earth.
No one knew about them, not even the angels in heaven, except him and his beloved Son, as we said before.
In the days when Solomon built the Lord’s temple in Jerusalem—for it was written this way: “No sound was heard in it, neither an axe nor an iron hammer.”
They were building it for twenty years. The king was building this temple so quietly that no sound of a craftsman working inside it could be heard.
Why, then? First, because they were building it for the Lord, in whose dwelling places no disturbance will appear.
For it is a wise king who builds it for the Lord God, who chose Solomon for himself to build him a house of this kind,
in silence, in keeping with the making of the first creation, which he created in silence, without any sound or disturbance.
For God was working through his own thought and his own reasoning.
He has no need of crowds, who disturb the place where they work.
God is not like this. Rather, his thought and his command are more than sufficient to accomplish every kind of craftsmanship.
Therefore, listen to what is written in the Exodus of Moses, when Moses was making the tabernacle and the ark of the covenant:
“See to it,” he said, “that you make everything according to the pattern you were shown on the mountain.”
Who, then, made them, except the command of God?
This is also how God will build his hidden temple for himself.
This is also what the wise Paul wrote about: “You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you.”
Again: “Do you not know that you are the temple of the Holy Spirit who is within you?”
One of the wise men of old also says, “The great altar of God is the heart of the wise person.”
For it was the hand and the power of God that created all creation. It was also this that created humanity.
Listen also to Isaiah speaking in the person of God: “Was it not my hand that laid the foundation of the earth? And it was my right hand that established heaven.”
“I will call them all, and they will stand together.”
And the blessed David also cries out, “It was his hands that formed the dry land.”
And again, in Hosea, he said, “It was my hand that created the host of heaven.”
And again, in Isaiah: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool for my feet.”
“What house will you build for me?” says the Lord.
“Was it not my hand that made all these things?”
It was also this hand that formed the first human being, Adam.
Therefore, after the formation of the first human being described in Genesis,
the righteous Job also says, “Remember that you formed me from clay, and I will return again to the earth.”
And again: “Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?”
“You clothed me with skin and flesh, and you bound me together with bones and sinews.”
“You placed life and mercy within me, and your care preserved my spirit.”
Since you have these within you, I know that you can do anything, and nothing is impossible for you.
Then again, David the psalmist says, “Your hands are what shaped me and made me.”
And again, “You are the one who brought me out of my mother’s womb.”
And again, “In secret, my bone was not hidden from you, since you made it in secret.”
He also says in Jeremiah, “Before I formed [?], before forming you in the womb, I knew you; and before you came out of the womb, I made you holy.”
But after all this, if it was God's hand that created all creation—heaven, earth, the sea, and everything in them—
then why were they going to perish and be dissolved amid great disturbance—creation, humanity, and Solomon's temple?
Again, the Lord says in the Gospel, “I am working, and my Father is working until now.”
As for the six days that God made, he made them with great delight, joy, and contentment.
And again, he spent six thousand years providing for the world through his commandments, his laws, and his holy prophets.
And the chief of all these things: his holy coming among us,
and all the suffering of his apostles, and all the provision for human needs, and the course of the heavenly lights.
And again, after all this, a single hour should suddenly overturn and destroy the whole creation.
And again, the six days that God spent creating the world—for in the blink of an eye all these things should perish and dissolve.
For it is he, the Lord of all and the Creator, Jesus Christ, who said in the Gospel, “Heaven and earth will pass away.”
And again, “But concerning that day and that hour, no one knows except the Father alone,” because they will not be able to bear the great turmoil that will occur.
Oh, this great sorrow! All the labors of this long age—that is, the ordering of things, the ministry of the angels, the service of the heavenly lights,
and the pouring down of dew upon the earth, the blowing of the winds!
the strength of the earth that it gives to human beings, the flow of the waters of the rivers—
all these things, then, a single hour should wipe out, and they should perish.
Why, then, would this single hour be able to cause all these evils, except through sin and disobedience?
It was the first transgression that cast humanity out of paradise, namely, disobedience.
It changed the world: it caused things that were not destined to happen to happen, while it prevented things that were destined to happen.
It made God, who is free from anger, become angry. It made the Father of joy grieve.
Who, then, did all these things? It was sin.
It is the enemy of every human being, this evil beast that kills souls, this plundering bird, this biting snake,
the consuming fire, this robber who plunders every soul—sin, this murderous barbarian, this turbulent harbor,
the desert road, this evil encounter—sin, which summons death and brings mourning.
The one who stirs up wars and lays waste to cities, destroys peoples, and makes the whole earth unfruitful.
He is also the one who causes the dew of heaven to be withheld. He also makes parents witness the death of their children and mourn over their loved ones.
It changes rivers, leads nations astray, and brings nations into territories that are not theirs.
Thorns and thistles came into being because of sin. Because of it, death reigned. Because of it, too, judgment took place in paradise, and rebukes in the place of joy.
Because of sin, too, weeping came into being in the age to come, and sorrow arose throughout all creation.
Because of it, the flood came upon the earth, as the floodgates of heaven poured out
their waters of wrath upon the earth, and the springs of the deep opened and gushed up their waters of vengeance.
Because of it, God considered wiping out all the creatures on the face of the whole earth.
It was the transgression of the Watchers, who are the giants, that brought the flood.
It was sin, defilement, and the practice of every kind of impurity that burned Sodom and Gomorrah.
The meddling of the people of Calneh caused people's languages to change, until they were scattered over the whole earth.
Pharaoh's sin and stubbornness destroyed the people of Egypt.
The lawlessness of idolatry wiped out the seven nations in the land of Canaan.
It was sin and disobedience to God that killed the six hundred thousand in Israel in the wilderness,
by sword, fire, and snakes, because they chose sin for themselves and abandoned the Lord their God. Because of all these things,
the Lord cries out through Isaiah: “For look, in my anger I will turn the sea into a desert,
and I will make the rivers a desert. Their fish will dry up because there is no water, and they will die of thirst.”
I will put darkness over heaven and make its covering like sackcloth.”
It was sin that did all these things. And because of it, this day will bring destruction in this single hour,
and it will destroy all the adornment of this long span of time since the creation of the world.
Let us also hear about the construction of the great temple that Solomon built in profound quiet: who was able to demolish it down to its foundations?
For it is written this way in the third book of Kingdoms about the temple that Solomon built for the name of the Lord.
behold, the God of Israel, for no sound of a horse was heard in it, nor an axe, nor the sound of any iron tool, since through his great wisdom
he set aside a place a little distance from the temple, and they worked in that place.
He did this because the sound of the craftsmen would have deafened the king's ears and prevented him from hearing the cases of those who came to him for judgment.
For God had given him peace, with no war around him and no attack from any direction.
Because of this, he had no concern except the affairs of the kingdom alone.
He would rise early every morning, go out to the place he had prepared, and sit there,
so that all affairs would continue to proceed in order, without any inactivity or neglect.
For this reason, he did not allow the craftsmen to work in the place he had established, since otherwise the place would have remained noisy and they would not have heard the king's words.
When he had finished building the house after twenty years, he held the dedication of the house of the Lord.
He entered the temple with all Israel beside him. He bent his knees before the Lord's altar, with his hands stretched out toward heaven.
He prayed in this way, saying, “Lord, God of Israel, if heaven and the heaven of heaven cannot contain you, would God really come and dwell with human beings?
Now, therefore, Lord, listen to the prayer that your servant offers to you, so that your eyes and your ears may be open toward this house.”
And, in short, after his supplication, the Lord spoke with him at the altar, saying: “I have heard the prayer you offered to me.”
“I do not dwell in houses made by human hands. But because of the labor you have undertaken,
if you keep my commandments and my judgments, which I have entrusted to you, my eyes and my ears will be open toward this house that you have built.
“If, then, you transgress my commandments, I will cast this great place away from me,
and it will be demolished and become a desert. Everyone passing by will be amazed, clap their hands, and whistle, saying, ‘Why have they done these things to this great place?’”
And they will say, ‘Because they abandoned the Lord, the God of their ancestors, and became slaves to other, foreign gods.’
Now see: after Solomon fell asleep, the people sinned and attached themselves to this evil companion, which is sin.
This is also what caused the first human being to sin in paradise and changed the world from the beginning.
It is also what demolished the temple of the Hebrews through the Chaldeans. Their name is interpreted as “those who scatter” or “those who destroy.”
Solomon spent twenty years building it with precious stones and a great, extensive workforce, consisting of the following:
Eighty thousand burden-bearers; [?] thirty thousand in Lebanon cutting timber; three thousand four hundred supervisors; eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain.
And after all this, this enemy, which is sin, caused them to demolish it in a few days.
So we will say: “Was it, then, for more than a whole year that the Chaldeans did these things to Jerusalem?”
Thus, because of sin, this single year undid the work of these twenty years.
What the Hebrews built, the Chaldeans demolished because of the people's lawlessness.
What they built in peace, they demolished amid great turmoil.
What Solomon built with wisdom, Zedekiah demolished through his lawlessness.
Rightly, then, the Lord put these words into Solomon's mouth for him to say: “Wise women build houses, but the foolish woman demolishes hers with her own hands.”
The blessed Paul also says: “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.”
All these things happened under Solomon, but the destructive overthrow happened under Zedekiah.
The sound of the axes was not heard while it was being built by Solomon the wise.
But the sound of axes and hammers shook Jerusalem as it was being dismantled because of Zedekiah’s folly.
After this, listen also to Saint Stephen saying, “Solomon built a house,
but the Most High does not dwell in something made by hand.” Where, then, will God dwell, when he says, “God will truly dwell with human beings”?
For this truly happened: our Lord Jesus Christ came from heaven and dwelt with us, wearing flesh like ours, apart from sin.
This holy and precious temple, which our Savior willingly wore.
This is also what David spoke about: “Your temple is holy and wonderful in righteousness.”
Truly, the holy Virgin Mary is a real wonder. No human being like her has been born on earth.
Mary, this temple that is more exalted and more honored than Solomon’s, is the one who became a house for the true God,
Jesus Christ, Jesus our Lord, through whom glory belongs to the Father, together with him and the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.
Of Basil, bishop.
